chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Makfuf, who said:

I wrote to him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), asking him about the ginger drink, and the rose water, and the mulberry jam, and the apple jam, and the quince jam, and the pomegranate jam. So he wrote: 'Permissible'.

key_terms.السِّكَنْجَبِين: Sikanjabin, a traditional vinegar-based drink often mixed with honey and herbs, here referring to a ginger-based variant
key_terms.الْجُلَّاب: Julab, a sweet rose-water syrup or drink
key_terms.رُبِّ: Rubb, a thick fruit syrup or jam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming fruit jams and drinks like ginger water and rose water in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Sahl ibn Ziyad, records a specific inquiry to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding the permissibility of various fruit-based beverages and preserves, including sikanjabin (ginger drink), julab (rose water), and jams from mulberry, apple, quince, and pomegranate. The Imam’s concise response of 'halal' establishes their general permissibility in Shia jurisprudence, reflecting the principle that foodstuffs are inherently pure unless proven otherwise. This ruling is significant for understanding the baseline status of processed fruit products in Islamic dietary law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ja’far Bin Ahad Al Makfouf who said,

‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the ginger drink, and the rose water, and the mulberry jam, and the apple jam, and the quince jam, and the pomegranate jam. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad al-Makfuf who has said the following: “

I once wrote to him, meaning, abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and asked about oxymel, rose water, jam of mulberry, apple, quince and pomegranate. He (the Imam) said in writing, ’It is lawful. 5 ”
